summary: Clarify configuration for concurrent keepalive SSE sessions and bulk ingest refill windows
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports frequent 429s observed during overlap between long-lived SSE keepalive sessions and periodic bulk ingest jobs. This customer has a dedicated pool and believes quota accounting is double-counting tokens when keepalive heartbeats coincide with bulk upload bursts. They are asking for recommended rate-pool/refill configurations and whether separate burst pools should be created for long-lived connections vs short bulk writes.

Impact:
- StreamSight sees intermittent 429s affecting telemetry ingestion for 30-60s windows during their nightly bulk imports.
- Real-time dashboards degrade because SSE heartbeats are intermittently rejected, causing reconnect storms.
- Customer is on a dedicated plan and needs guidance to avoid impacting SLA-bound pipelines.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-34) in prod-us-east, fallback to eu-west.
- Long-lived SSE connections for real-time telemetry (~4k concurrent connections, 1 keepalive/sec).
- Bulk ingest jobs: 120 concurrent workers doing chunked uploads in batches every 5 minutes.

Steps to reproduce (as described by customer):
1. Spin up long-lived SSE clients to sustain ~4k keepalive messages/sec.
2. Trigger scheduled bulk ingest (120 workers) that push 1000 small files concurrently over a 30s window.
3. Observe 429s on SSE endpoints and some bulk worker retries for 30-90s.

Observed logs/snippets supplied by customer:
- "429 Too Many Requests - token window exhausted (route: /v1/stream/sse)"
- Console trace: "refill-window: 60s, burst-pool: standard, priority: background"
- Customer-side: increased reconnects and backoff loops in telemetry clients

Requested outcome:
- Clear recommended configuration to avoid soft-throttles when long-lived sessions run concurrently with bursty ingest jobs.
- If separation of pools is required, steps to configure on Dedicated and suggested threshold values.
- Any console or telemetry queries they can run to validate set-up.
comments: 2026-03-13 09:12 - Mira Chen (reporter): Opened ticket after customer provided initial logs and console screenshots. Customer is asking for explicit config examples for Dedicated pools.

2026-03-13 13:45 - Diego Martinez (support): Acknowledged and asked for ingestion job timings, heartbeat interval sample, and tenant-id. Requested retention of sample pcap and server trace for 429 window.

2026-03-13 15:02 - StreamSight (customer): Provided tenant-id TS-772, heartbeat interval 1s, bulk job schedule wave at 02:00 UTC with 30s spike, attached console export showing refill-window=60s and priority=background.

2026-03-13 17:30 - Diego Martinez: Noted this looks like refill-interval misalignment and priority-lane borrowing. Asked Eng rate-limiter to confirm whether keepalive heartbeats are accounted against the same token bucket as bulk uploads for dedicated pools.

2026-03-14 08:20 - SRE (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed current dedicated implementation uses a shared tenant-level token bucket by default unless a route-specific burst pool is configured. Suggested two quick mitigations and a longer-term config.
investigation_notes: Checked dedicated pool TS-34 metrics (ingest-orchestrator). CPU and GPU are healthy; spikes correlate with bulk job windows.
Rate-limiter logs show SSE heartbeat requests countable as 'interactive' path but were not marked as high-priority; they were consuming tenant token bucket during spike.
Observed refill-window configured to 60s with smoothing enabled; bulk jobs concentrated tokens into a short period, leading to temporary exhaustion for interactive flows.

Hypothesis: keepalive heartbeats, although low-cost individually, create sustained drain that prevents token smoothing from cushioning bulk spikes, resulting in short soft 429 windows when refill throttles align with bulk ingestion pulses.

Confirmed there is a configuration path to create an isolated burst pool for long-lived connections or to set an exemption pool for SSE heartbeats in Dedicated; requires console and config change plus a brief rollout to rate-limiter config (no code change).
resolution: Workaround provided: 1) Create separate burst pool for SSE route and mark it as high-availability with small refill (e.g., burst_capacity=6000 tokens, refill_interval=30s) and priority=interactive. 2) Configure bulk ingest route to use a distinct background pool with larger refill smoothing (e.g., burst_capacity=200000 tokens, refill_interval=300s) and priority=background. 3) Advise customer to add exponential jitter on bulk job start times to spread load. Implementation steps: console -> Dedicated pools -> Add rate-pool 'sse-heartbeat' scoped to route '/v1/stream/sse' then add 'bulk-ingest' pool scoped to '/v1/uploads' and bind to tenant TS-772. Follow-up: we've created a docs PR and an internal runbook entry (see related_confluence_pages). SRE will coordinate a safe rollout window (non-peak) to apply the config. Customer confirmed they will trial the config in their staging environment before prod change. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rate-limiter/pull/418. Follow-ups: create a Compass console template for Dedicated customers with mixed long-lived and batch traffic and add a note to onboarding for dedicated pools.
